texts.preamble: Sh.Priya Dutt Sharma vs State on 16 May, 2019 In The Court Of Ms. Poonam A. Bamba District & Sessions Judge, New Delhi In the matter of : Fsat No.18/2016 Sh.Priya Dutt Sharma M/s Navin Dairy Shop No.313/73, F, Anand Nagar Inder Lok,Delhi35. Vs 1. State, Through Commissioner Department of Food Safety, Govt. of Nct of Delhi A20, Lawrence Road Delhi110035. 2. Sh. S.K.Nagpal Designated Officer Department of Food Safety Govt. of Nct of Delhi A20, Lawrence Road Delhi110035. 3. Sh.Ashok Kumar Singh Food Safety Officer Department of Food Safety Govt. of Nct of Delhi A20, Lawrence Road Delhi110035. ..... Fsat No. 18/2016 M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. Appeal Against The Order Dated 03.05.2013 Of Ld. Additional District Magistrate(Central)/ Adjudicating Officer, New Delhi. Date of filing of appeal : 30.05.2013
texts.facts: Vide this judgment, I shall dispose of the present appeal, challenging the order dated 03.05.2013 ("the impugned order" in short) of Ld. on 16 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88250504/ 1 Magistrate (Central)("ADM" in short), New Delhi directing the appellant to pay a penalty of Rs.1,50,000/, under Section 51 of The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006("FSS Act" in short) for violation of Section 26(2)(ii) of FSS Act read with Section 3(1) (zx) of FSS Act for selling sub standard food/milk. 2.0 Briefly stating, the facts as per appeal are that : (i) on 27.06.2012, Food Safety Officer ("FSO" in short), purchased sample of "Toned Milk" from Sh.Priya Dutt Sharma from the premises of M/s Navin M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. Dairy, Shop No.313/73, F, Anand Nagar, Inder Lok, Delhi110035 where the said food article was found stored for sale for human consumption. The sample consisted of approx. 2Litre (2000ml) of "Toned Milk"(ready for sale) taken from an open steel drum having declaration "Toned Milk" on it; (ii) the sample of toned milk was taken after proper mixing with the help of clean & dry measure by rotating in all possible directions i.e. up & down, clock wise and anticlockwise several times. The sample of toned milk was divided into four equal parts then and there by putting into four clean and dry glass bottles and 40 drops of formalin was added in each bottle with the help of clean and dry dropper. Each bottle containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to the provisions of FSS Act and Rules/Regulations framed thereunder; (iii) one counterpart of the sample under sealed cover was sent to Food Analyst. Other two counterparts were deposited with Designated Officer. As the FBO did not M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. request to send the fourth counter part for analysis from NABL Acreedited Laboratory , the fourth sealed counterpart was also deposited with the Designated Officer; (iv) the Food Analyst vide his report dated 09.07.2012 opined "The sample is substandard because milk solids not fat is less than the prescribed minimum limit of 8.5%; (v) the Designated Officer concerned sent a copy of the Food Analyst report to the FBO Sh.Priya Dutt Sharma of M/s Navin Dairy/ the appellant giving them an opportunity to file an appeal against the report of the Food Analyst u/S 46(4) for sending one part of the same to the Referral Lab, if so desired by him. The FBO appeared before the Designated Officer and requested to send the sample to Referral Laboratory; (vi) the Director Referral Food Laboratory, Mysore vide Certificate No.315/FSSA/2012 dated 23.08.2012 reported that sample is substandard as defined u/S 3(1) M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. (zx) FSS Act and does not conform to the standard laid down for toned milk under the provisions of The Food Safety and Standards(Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, Sh.Priya Dutt Sharma vs State on 16 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88250504/ 2 2011("FSS(FPS & FA) Regulations" in short) thereof, in that: "Milk fat content falls below the minimum standard limit" (vii) in view of the above, an application/complaint under rule 3.1.1(3) of The Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011("FSSR" in short) was filed before the Ld. ADM; (viii) after enquiry, the Ld. ADM passed the impugned order dated 03.05.2013. 3.0 The appellant has challenged the impugned order inter alia on the grounds that: (i) no independent witness was joined at the time of lifting of the sample in violation of Section 38(7) FSS Act; M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. (ii) Rule 2.4.1(7) of FSSR which requires that the sample food article has to be taken in clean and dry bottles/jar etc. was not complied with. No such statement has been made by the FSO in his Abhiyog Pattar/no document filed before the court; (iii) the sample was not taken in a proper manner by the FSO. Hence, correct analysis was not possible which could be inferred from the contradictory reports of Food Analyst and Director Referral Laboratory; such contradictory reports also reflect possibility of there being an error of judgment in analysis by the Food Analyst or Director Referral Laboratory; (iv) no witness either from the department or otherwise was examined by the Ld.ADM. The impugned order has been passed on the basis of the complaint/application and other un exhibited documents without any supporting affidavit by the FSO. Thus,enquiry proceedings were not conducted properly; (v) sanction is bad in law as it suffers from non M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. application of mind and consideration of facts by the Designated Officer; 4.0 Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor sought dismissal of this appeal with heavy cost pleading that it lacks merit. The impugned order has been rightly passed by the Ld.ADM on the basis of the evidence on record. 3 6.0 The appellant's challenge to the impugned order is two fold. Firstly, on the ground that there is variation in the findings in the Food Analyst's report and the report of Referral Food Laboratory; and that no penalty could have been imposed on the appellant in view of contradictory reports.
texts.arguments: The appellant's second challenge to the impugned order is, that proper procedure as per law was not followed. Once the opinion of the M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. 8.1 Before I deal with the rival contentions, let me refer here the Section 47 FSS Act in this repsect, which reads as under: "47.Sampling and analysis.(1) When a Food Safety Officer takes a sample of food for analysis, he shall (a) give notice in writing of his intention to have it so analysed to the person from whom he has taken the sample and to the person, if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed; (b) except in special cases as may be provided by rules made under this Act, divide the sample into four parts and mark and seal or fasten up each part in such a manner as its nature permits and take the signature or thumb impression of the person from whom the sample has been taken in such place and in such manner as may be prescribed by the Central Government: Provided that where such person refuses to sign or put his thumb impression, the Food Safety Officer shall call upon one or more witnesses and take his signature or thumb impression, in lieu of the signature or thumb impression of such person; (c) (i) send one of the parts for analysis to the Food Analyst under intimation to the Designated Officer; (ii) send two parts to the Designated Officer for keeping these in safe custody; and (iii) send the remaining part for analysis to an accredited laboratory, if M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. so requested by the food business operator, under intimation to the Designated Officer: Provided that if the test reports received under subclauses (i) and (iii) are found to be at variance, then the Designated Officer shall send one part of the sample kept in his custody, to referral laboratory for analysis, whose decision thereon shall be final." Sh . Priya Dutt Sharma vs State on 16 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88250504/ 5 8.1.1 It would also be pertinent to refer here to Rule 2.4.6 of FSSR, which reads as under: "2.4.6 Appeal to the Designated Officer 1.When an appeal as provided under subsection (4) of section 46 is preferred to the Designated Officer by the Food Business Operator against the report of the Food Analyst, the Designated Officer, shall if he so decides, within thirty days from the receipt of such appeal after considering the material placed before him and after giving an opportunity to Food Business Operator to be heard shall forward one part of the sample to the referral lab. While dealing with the similar contention (under the old Act) as raised in the present appeal, the Hon'ble High Court in Subhash Chander v. State(Delhi Administration) Delhi ,1983 (4) DRJ 100, observed that: Sh.Priya Dutt Sharma vs State on 16 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88250504/ 6 "7.It has repeatedly been held by the supreme court that the certificate of the Director supersedes the report of the public analyst and is to be treated as conclusive evidence of its contents. 8.4 It may be mentioned that in subsequent judgment, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. Pawan Kumar Saraf, AIR 1999 SC 738 dealt with similar issue of finality of Certificate of Central Food Laboratory. In that case, the Food Analyst found the sample of compounded Asafoetida to be adulterated as it did not conform to the prescribed standard. Whereas, the Central Food Laboratory vide its certificate found the sample to be in conformity with the prescribed standard. Accused approached the Hon'ble High Court in revision. The Municipal Corporation challenged the same before the Hon'ble Supreme Court. The Hon'ble Supreme Court after considering the relevant provisions under PFA Act observed as under: "9.....Sub section (3) of Section 13 is important in this context and is extracted below : "The certificate issued by the Director of the Central Food Laboratory under sub section (2B) shall supersede the report given by the public analyst under sub section (1)." 10.When the statute says that certificate shall supersede the report, it means that the report would stand annulled or obliterated. The word "supersede" in law, means "obliterate, [LEAKAGE_MASK], annul, replace, make void or inefficacious or useless, repeal", (vide Black's Law Dictionary, M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. 5th Edn.). Once the Certificate of the Director of Central Food Laboratory reaches the court, the Report of the Public Analyst stands displaced and what may remain is only a fossil of it. The material portion of the proviso is quoted below : Sh.Priya Dutt Sharma vs State on 16 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88250504/ 7 "Provided that any document purporting to be a certificate signed by the Director of the Central Food Laboratory........shall be final and conclusive evidence of the facts stated therein." 12.If a fact is declared by a statute as final and conclusive, its impact is crucial because no party can then give evidence for the purpose of disproving the fact. This is the import of Section 4 of the Evidence Act which defines three kinds of presumptions among which the last is "conclusive proof. "When one fact is declared by this Act to be conclusive proof of another, the court shall, on proof of the one fact, regard the other as proved, and shall not allow evidence to be given for the purpose of disproving it." 13.Thus the legal impact of a certificate of the Director of Central Food Laboratory is threefold. It annuls or replaces the report of the Public Analyst, it gains finality regarding the quality and standard of the food article involved in the case and it becomes irrefutable so far as the facts stated therein are concerned....." M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. 8.5 Similar issue whether it is open to the accused to plead that if there is any variance between the two reports, the prosecution must explain the said variance or otherwise fail, came up for consideration before the Full Bench of the Hon'ble High Court of Gujarat in Prahlad Bhai Amba Lal Patel vs State of Gujarat, 1984(2)FAC 26. The Hon'ble court while relying upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex court in Andhra Pradesh Grain & Seeds Merchant Association v. Union of India, AIR 1971 SC 246 and Chetumal vs State of M.P., AIR 1981 SC 1387, held that: "7.....Proviso to Section 13(5) also indicates that what is stated in the later certificate issued by the Director would be final and conclusive evidence of the facts stated in the said certificate.....Once this type of conclusive evidence emerges on record, whatever might have been contraindicated regarding the concerned ingredients of the sample as found in the prior report of the public analyst would be totally pushed out of the arena of contest and cannot be looked at. If that is so, there would be no question of considering any variance between the results of the tests carried out by the public analyst on the one hand and the Director of the Central Food Laboratory on the other visavis two parts of the same sample..... But if one of the reports is wholly pushed out of record as enjoined by Section 13(3) read with Section 13(5), there is no question of resorting to the exercise of comparison between the contents of these two reports with a view to finding out the supposed variance between the existing and operative report of the Director and earlier M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. report of the public analyst which has ceased to exist on record." 8.6 Now let me refer to the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Kashi Nath vs State,2005(2)FAC 219, relied upon by Ld.Counsel for the appellant in support of his contention that variation in two reports shows that the sample sent for examination was not representative. The said expert in his cross examination stated that sodium chloride, an inorganic salt contributes towards total ash only; and that sodium chloride is Class I preservative; and if sodium chloride is subtracted (3.4%) from total ash content of 9.86% by weight, it(sample) meets the requirement of total ash content of 7% by weight as per PFA Act M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. and Rules. 8.6.1 In view of the above deposition of the expert, the Hon'ble Court although noted (in para 13 of the judgment) that there can be no quarrel about the impact of certificate of Director of Central Food Laboratory i.e. it annuls or replaces the report of the Public Analyst, it gains finality regarding the quality and standard of the food article involved in the case and it becomes irrefutable so far as the facts stated therein are concerned. It went on to observe that considering the ratio in MCD vs Bishan Sarup,ILR 1970(1) Delhi 518, it would still be open for the accused to establish that the sample tested was not a representative one and if the variation in the two reports is substantial enough, then the Public Analyst's report can certainly be looked into to establish this variation. 8.6.2 In view of the same, the judgments in Raj Kumar vs State of Punjab, 2003(1) FAC, P.121 Punjab & Haryana High Court and State of Himachal Pradesh vs Kamlesh Chand, 2002(2) FAC P.315, relied upon by the appellant are of no assistance to him. The case law i.e. State of Gujarat vs Anil Champak Lal Sha & Anr., 2007(2) FAC P.130, Gujarat High Court and Shew Chander Mhatur & Anr. Vs State of Assam & Anr. 1991(1) FAC P.9, Gauhati High Court relied upon by the appellant in this respect, is hardly of any help. "3.Definitions (1)..... (zx)substandard an article of food shall be deemed to be substandard if it does not meet the specified standards but not so as to render the article of food unsafe;" M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. 14.1 It may be mentioned that Sections 26 FSS Act which lays down the responsibilities of the FBO, inter alia enjoins upon every FBO, to ensure that food article, whether produced, sold, distributed, stored etc. under his control shall satisfy the requirements of the FSS Act and the Rules and Regulations framed thereunder. Section 26 FSS Act reads as under: "26.Responsibilities of the food business operator.(1) Every food business operator shall ensure that the articles of food satisfy the requirements of this Act and the rules and regulations made thereunder at all stages of production, processing, import, distribution and sale within the businesses under his control. (2)No food business operator shall himself or by any person on his behalf manufacture, store, sell or distribute any article of food (i) which is unsafe; or (ii) which is misbranded or substandard or contains extraneous matter....." 15.0 No averment regarding quantum of penalty has been M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. made by the appellant.
